items.title: These mid-cap stocks with ‘Strong Buy’ & ‘Buy’ recos can rally over 25%, according to analysts
items.description: Here’s one thing to watch for in the next few weeks: How does the street treat disappointments in the mid-cap segment? If the reaction is limited to the stock concerned and does not sustain beyond one or two trading sessions, it can be taken as a bullish sign. If, however, the disappointment with one stock leads the street to punish the whole sector in that segment, it suggests there are more institutional investors waiting to sell. It would also indicate that the market is top heavy.

items.title: Shiprocket soars 48% on debut, erases valuation cut
items.description: Shiprocket shares debuted on Wednesday at a notable premium compared to their IPO price. The e-commerce logistics firm experienced a robust closing surge on the Bombay Stock Exchange. This impressive market entry effectively reversed a previous decline in valuation prior to its public listing. Early backer Bertelsmann benefited greatly, witnessing a remarkable increase in their stake. Investors enthusiastically oversubscribed the company's initial public offering.

items.title: Sebi bars two entities for 'manipulating' CAS
items.description: Sebi barred Copthall Mauritius Investment and Mansi Share and Stock Broking from securities market access.  The regulator alleged manipulation of the Sensex during the new closing auction session.  Sharp and unusual movements were detected in the index on August 13 expiry day.  These actions aimed to benefit from outstanding Sensex options positions, Sebi stated.  The entities allegedly generated wrongful gains totaling over Rs 3.6 crore.

items.title: D-Street poised for a positive start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
items.description: Nifty declined for a seventh session, influenced by elevated crude oil prices. Analysts anticipate continued pressure due to global weakness and geopolitical tensions. The India VIX, a fear gauge, saw a slight decrease to 11.32 levels. Foreign and domestic institutional investors showed net buying activity on Wednesday. The Indian rupee weakened against the dollar but saw central bank intervention.

items.title: Stocks in news: Hyundai Motor India, BSE, HEG, Hexaware Tech and Oil India
items.description: Indian equity markets extended their losing streak to a seventh consecutive session, with the Nifty50 closing lower at 24,078.30. Key corporate developments are expected to influence Thursday's trade, including Hyundai Motor India's planned price increase, Aditya Infotech's fundraising approval, and BSE's agreement with MSCI for index futures and options. Other companies like HEG, Ceigall India, and HDFC Life Insurance also saw significant announcements.

items.title: Sebi plans comprehensive review of rules governing SME IPOs
items.description: Sebi plans a comprehensive review of IPO rules for small and medium companies.  Market making and underwriting systems are identified as areas needing attention.  A working group has submitted its report on the SME platform to the regulator.  Sebi will soon release a consultation paper regarding the SME platform.  The regulator also aims to support global fund management activities from India.

items.title: Nifty price-to-book ratio hits 6-year low, but market may not be cheap
items.description: The Nifty's price-to-book ratio has slid below three for the first time in six years, showcasing the banking sector's struggles alongside rising book values. With banks and financial services playing a crucial role in the Nifty's composition, the recent consolidation of financials has notably influenced valuation metrics. It is now essential for investors to prioritize earnings growth and future profitability projections.

items.title: RDIF AIF selection expected to be completed in two weeks
items.description: The government is in the final stages of choosing alternative investment firms for the research fund, with the decision expected to wrap up in the coming fortnight. Meanwhile, funds are actively being allocated to other selected firms for investment purposes. Robust safeguards are implemented to ensure protection for both public and private capital, reinforcing transparency and accountability in the fund's management.

items.title: India may see family wealth worth $1.5 trillion change hands in 10 years
items.description: India anticipates a significant intergenerational wealth transfer exceeding one trillion dollars.  Family wealth is becoming more institutionalized with formal governance structures.  This trend will expand the alternatives market significantly in the coming decade.  India's billionaire and ultra-high-net-worth individual numbers are projected to increase.  Exits and liquidity events are driving demand for wealth management services.

items.title: No takers: Public sector banks put ₹39,000 cr of bad loans up for sale again
items.description: Public sector banks offered many bad loans previously for sale.  Nearly eighty percent of these loans were repeat sale attempts.  Indian Overseas Bank and Indian Bank led these repeated offerings.  Private sector banks showed a sharp contrast with few repeat sales.  This highlights challenges in selling large legacy corporate accounts.

items.title: SC rejects GST department review plea, telecom firms get relief on tower tax credit
items.description: The Supreme Court rejected a review petition from the GST Department.  This decision confirms telecom towers are movable property for tax credit.  Bharti Airtel and Indus Tower received significant relief from this ruling.  The court found no error in its previous order regarding tax eligibility.  This reaffirms the principle of allowing credit for business inputs.

items.title: RBI deputy governor Murmu calls for focus on meaningful financial inclusion
items.description: Banks must measure financial inclusion by effective usage and informed decisions.  Technology shifts and consumer behavior necessitate responsive banking systems.  Digital inclusion deepens, and AI helps recognize capability across diverse groups.  Institutions need skilled people to challenge models and oversee external providers.  Prudence requires pooled intelligence and credible alternatives for system resilience.

items.title: Bonus issue alert! Last day to buy Goodluck India shares for 2:1 bonus reward. How will dividend payout be impacted?
items.description: Goodluck India in July announced its maiden bonus issue in the ratio of 2:1. Under the proposal, eligible shareholders will receive two bonus equity shares of face value Rs 2 each for every one equity share held as of the record date, which will be announced separately.

items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy LIC Housing Finance, Hitachi Energy among 38 stocks for dividends. How many do you own?
items.description: Under Sebi's T+1 settlement cycle, investors need to purchase a company’s shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by the record date (August 21), making them eligible for the dividend.

items.title: Negative Breakout: These 8 stocks cross below their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed below their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 19, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Trading below the 200 DMA is considered a negative signal because it indicates that the stock's price is below its long-term trend line. Traders use the 200 DMA as a key indicator to determine the overall trend in a particular stock. Take a look:

items.title: Stocks to buy: 4 FMCG stocks to buy with up to 27% upside potential. Do you own any?
items.description: Axis Securities in its latest note pointed out that Q1 marked another quarter of improving consumption momentum, with most FMCG companies delivering high-single to double-digit topline growth. Rural and urban demand remained resilient, supported by improving consumer sentiment, premiumisation, deeper distribution and the recent GST rate cuts. The brokerage noted that Q1 marked the second consecutive quarter of sequential improvement in demand, although erratic monsoons affected select summer-centric categories.

items.title: Longest on record! Nifty fails to cross previous day's high for 12 straight days. Will it surpass today?
items.description: The Nifty index has struggled to break its previous day's high for an astonishing twelve sessions in a row. This unusual sequence is coinciding with investors evaluating robust quarterly earnings against looming global uncertainties. Market trajectories are now closely tied to the stability of crude oil supplies and liquidity in the domestic arena.

items.title: Sebi bets on trading reforms to reverse  foreign capital flight
items.description: India's market regulator is poised to introduce substantial rule amendments aimed at boosting foreign investments. The planned reforms intend to lower collateral demands and stimulate interest in longer-term derivatives. With foreign investment in Indian stocks hitting a seventeen-year low, the Securities and Exchange Board of India will engage with industry players prior to rolling out these transformative measures, ultimately hoping to enhance India's position in global stock market rankings.

items.title: ICICI Prudential AMC among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 19, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 2% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Why is market rising today? Sensex rallies 500 points, Nifty tops 24,200. 5 key factors behind market rebound
items.description: On Thursday, Indian stock markets made a robust comeback, ending a series of losses. The Sensex and Nifty indices surged due to a positive mood among investors, influenced by declining US bond yields and notable short-covering activities. The broader markets also reflected this upswing, with midcap and smallcap stocks gaining ground. Notably, giants like Infosys and TCS emerged as key contributors to this rally.

items.title: Blue Star among 4 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of August 19, there was a notable surge in futures open interest for four stocks in the NSE F&O pack, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 11% as compared to the previous trade. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies a substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions within the futures market.

items.title: SKF India among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals, indicating possible uptrend
items.description: On August 19, five stocks with a market cap over Rs 10,000 crore and gains of more than 4% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Why Jefferies sees limited upside in Bajaj Housing Finance despite its fast-growing loan book
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on Bajaj Housing Finance with a Hold rating and Rs 92 target, citing limited upside from premium valuations despite strong growth prospects. It expects AUM to grow at a 23% CAGR and earnings per share at 20% through FY29, while return on assets stays near 2% and return on equity improves to 13.6%.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Nomura maintains neutral stance on Maruti Suzuki; Goldman Sachs recommends buy on Godrej Consumer
items.description: Top global brokerages have issued fresh calls across sectors. Nomura maintained Neutral on Maruti Suzuki expecting further price hikes, while Goldman Sachs recommended Buy on Godrej Consumer Products with a 26% upside. Citi initiated a positive catalyst watch on Fortis Healthcare, seeing potential 29% upside.

items.title: Credent Connect shares make strong market debut, list at 90% premium over IPO price on NSE SME platform
items.description: Credent Connect N Care shares made a blockbuster debut on the NSE SME platform, listing at a 90% premium over the IPO price. The Rs 93.90-crore issue was subscribed 153.13 times, with strong demand across investor categories. The company plans to use IPO proceeds for working capital, capex, debt repayment and subsidiary funding.

items.title: Muthoot Finance, Manappuram, other gold financier stocks jump up to 4% as gold prices rise above Rs 1.58 lakh/10 grams
items.description: Shares of gold loan companies Muthoot Finance, Manappuram Finance and IIFL Finance rose as much as 4% as gold prices surged following the US Treasury’s decision to increase longer-dated bond buybacks. Rising gold prices can boost the value of collateral pledged against gold loans.

items.title: Shiprocket shares jump 6% as Goldman Sachs acquires Rs 53 crore stake. Time to buy or book profits?
items.description: Shiprocket shares rose sharply on Thursday, extending gains after a blockbuster market debut. The rally came amid strong institutional interest, with Goldman Sachs buying shares worth Rs 52.7 crore in a bulk deal. Analysts remain positive but advise existing investors to consider partial profit-booking and fresh buyers to await dips.

items.title: Strides Pharma Science shares jump 9% after USFDA EIR for Bengaluru facility
items.description: Strides Pharma Science shares rise sharply on Thursday after the USFDA issued an Establishment Inspection Report (EIR) for its Bengaluru facility, concluding a recent cGMP inspection. The inspection ended with five observations, which the company addressed through corrective actions. The regulatory closure offers relief after the stock’s recent weakness.

items.title: Milky Mist Dairy Food shares slip 4% after sharp post-listing rally
items.description: Milky Mist Dairy Food shares came under profit-booking pressure after gaining 42% over two sessions following their market debut. Despite strong revenue growth, improving profitability and a leadership position in value-added dairy, analysts cautioned against chasing the stock after its sharp post-listing rally and premium valuation.

items.title: Sugar stocks Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar, Balrampur Chini, others rally up to 8% after govt tightens stock limits
items.description: Sugar stocks rallied up to 8% after the government tightened inventory limits for dealers amid record-high sugar prices. Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar led gains, while Balrampur Chini and other stocks also advanced. Concerns over domestic and Brazilian supply, rising festive-season demand and a possible cut in import duties have further supported prices.

items.title: Can Turtlemint Fintech shares rally to Rs 190? Why Jefferies initiated coverage on the stock
items.description: Jefferies has initiated coverage on Turtlemint Fintech Solutions with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 190, implying 37% upside. The brokerage expects revenue to grow at a 38% CAGR over three years, driven by higher premiums and take-rates.

items.title: Titagarh Rail Systems shares gain 3% after Indian Railways' approval for traction motor supply
items.description: Titagarh Rail Systems shares rose after Indian Railways approved the company as a vendor for supplying three-phase asynchronous traction motors for locomotives. The approval allows Titagarh to supply up to 1,200 traction motors annually, boosting its prospects in the railway equipment segment.

items.title: Coforge shares jump 3% after IT major launches private equity unit
items.description: Coforge shares climbed on Thursdat after the IT services company launched a dedicated Private Equity business unit to help funds drive operational transformation and value creation across portfolio companies. The new vertical will leverage Coforge’s acquisition integration expertise and AI capabilities to support portfolio optimisation, EBITDA growth and technology-led transformation.

items.title: Power Finance Corporation and REC shares fall up to 3% after Morgan Stanley downgrade
items.description: PFC and REC shares fell on Thursday after Morgan Stanley downgraded both stocks to Equal-Weight and cut their target prices. The brokerage flagged slower loan growth and lowered earnings estimates for FY28 and FY29. The downgrade comes ahead of the proposed PFC-REC merger, with both stocks already under pressure.

items.title: Jefferies raises Emmvee Photovoltaic Power target price to Rs 440: Can the stock rally further?
items.description: Jefferies has raised its target price for Emmvee Photovoltaic Power to Rs 440 from Rs 400, while retaining its Buy rating, implying around 31% upside. The brokerage is bullish on the company’s strong solar PV value-chain presence, healthy order book and expansion plans

items.title: NSE said to plan allowing trading in its shares on its own platform
items.description: NSE may allow its shares to trade on its own platform after listing on rival BSE, potentially boosting liquidity and paving the way for inclusion in Nifty indexes. The proposal was discussed with global investors during IPO roadshows. However, current rules don’t permit exchange self-listing, meaning NSE would need Sebi approval. The IPO is targeted for September.

items.title: Explained: How a JP Morgan unit and a Mumbai-based stock broking firm allegedly manipulated Sensex during CAS
items.description: The regulator flagged three sharp Sensex spikes, including a 362-point jump in two seconds and a 405-point surge in 28 seconds, as the index’s CAS closing price moved to around 78,080 from a 3:15 pm reference of 77,829.60.

items.title: IT stocks extend gains for second day; Coforge, Infosys, Persistent Systems rise up to 3%
items.description: IT stocks extended gains for the second straight session, with Coforge and Persistent Systems leading the rally. Infosys, Wipro, TCS and Tech Mahindra also traded higher, lifting the Nifty IT index nearly 2%. The rally was driven by value buying amid a weaker rupee, with Indian IT stocks continuing to outperform global tech peers.

items.title: MCX shares jump 4% as gold, silver futures rise. What lies ahead after a 900% rally in 3 years?
items.description: MCX shares jumped over 4% as gold, silver and copper futures rose following a US Treasury liquidity support announcement. The stock has delivered stellar returns of around 900% in three years. UBS upgraded MCX to ‘Buy’ and raised its target to Rs 3,800, while HDFC Securities retained its ‘Buy’ rating, citing regulatory easing and strong growth potential

items.title: Zaggle Prepaid shares jump 3% , extend 3-day rally to 16%. What's driving the rally?
items.description: Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services shares rose on Thursday, extending their three-day rally to 16% after Vijay Kedia-backed Kedia Securities acquired 20 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 33 crore. The stock’s sharp rebound comes days after it plunged 20% following a weak Q1FY27 earnings report.

items.title: 14 smallcap stocks zoom up to 217% in last 6 months, 6 turn multibaggers. Do you own any?
items.description: In the last six months, the benchmark Nifty 50 fell around 5.5%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 bucked the trend, surging nearly 15%. But the broader smallcap index tells only part of the story.The real action was among individual stocks. Nearly 70 smallcap stocks gained more than 25% during this period, with the top 14 performers delivering returns ranging from 60% to a staggering 217%. Even more striking, six stocks more than doubled investors’ wealth in just six months.While the broader market struggled, these smallcaps delivered a remarkable wealth-creation story. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: India’s family office wealth to grow 1.5x in three years as ultra-rich shift strategies: Report
items.description: Wealthy families in India are shifting their fortunes into advanced investment mechanisms, with family office assets expected to rise markedly in the coming three years. This growth is fueled by rising wealth levels and innovative investment approaches. Families are increasingly directing significant resources toward alternative assets and forward-looking industries. To optimize their operations, contemporary family offices are leveraging technology and adopting professional governance practices.

items.title: Why Zerodha’s Nithin Kamath wants fintech founders to rethink trading in the age of AI
items.description: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has urged fintech founders to rethink the future of trading and investing as AI, evolving market structures, regulations and emerging technologies reshape financial markets. He said brokers could eventually become little more than a “pipe” between customers and exchanges, while Rainmatter is again doubling down on fintech investments.

items.title: BSE shares fall over 3% from day’s high after report says NSE weighs trading shares on own platform
items.description: BSE shares fell over 3% from the day’s high after a report said NSE may seek permission to trade its shares on its own platform following its proposed IPO listing on BSE. The move could boost liquidity for NSE shares, while potentially shifting trading volumes and affecting BSE’s market position.

items.title: Market wrap:  Eternal Kotak Bank, HCL Tech, InterGlobe top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian equities snapped a seven-session losing streak as Nifty gained 0.64% and Sensex surged 628 points, aided by relief in global bond yields. Market breadth turned positive, while analysts identified 24,100-24,000 as crucial support and 24,300 as immediate resistance.

items.title: Jefferies favours two-wheeler stocks over four-wheeler stocks as earnings gap widens
items.description: Jefferies prefers two-wheeler stocks over passenger vehicle makers, citing stronger volume growth, resilient margins and improving earnings. TVS Motor Company and Eicher Motors remain its top picks, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Hyundai Motor India carry Underperform ratings amid rising competition, higher discounts and a weaker earnings outlook.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.
